items.title: OpenAI split its lineup in two
items.oneliner: OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra beats its predecessor by 5.2 points at under one-third the cost.

items.title: Microsoft flooded the market with models
items.oneliner: Microsoft shipped seven MAI models, including a cheaper Code 2 that claims 98% of prior coding quality.

items.title: RadixArk pushed RL into agent benchmarks
items.oneliner: DaisyRose-27B doubled Terminal-Bench 4.1 from 5.6% to 12%, showing targeted RL still moves hard agent tasks.

items.title: Energy-based reasoning got real numbers
items.oneliner: Energy-Based Reasoners claim 385x cheaper inference, hinting that reasoning gains may come from architecture, not just scale.

items.title: Java got a Base64 remote exploit
items.oneliner: Java4Shell turns OpenJDK's Base64 decoder into unauthenticated RCE, a nasty reminder that memory safety still has escape hatches.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 needs patching now
items.oneliner: Critical NGINX HTTP/2 RCE bugs hit versions 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, so internet-facing fleets need emergency patch windows.

items.title: Windows is watching your coding agents
items.oneliner: Windows 11 tracks executables like codex.exe and python.exe by default, making dev-tool telemetry an OS-level product decision.

items.title: PyPI tightened package upload rules
items.oneliner: PyPI now rejects risky source distributions, closing parser-differential tricks before they become the next supply-chain incident.

items.title: Google open-sourced its giant repo speedup
items.oneliner: Google cut Android checkout from 30 minutes to under 8 seconds, then open-sourced the system behind it.

items.title: Vector search moved into the lakehouse
items.oneliner: Lakegres adds vector search directly on Iceberg, Hudi, and Open tables, reducing another reason to stand up a separate vector database.
